stop_condition: Done when (1) the STATED COVERAGE RESIDUAL and four-shape history are judged for honesty against the file's own contents - no overstated coverage anywhere in the spec; (2) the 'REMOVED, not re-guarded' claim is verified mechanically; (3) all five anti-overreach outcomes are confirmed with actual output. Then either a finding at or above high, or verdict=approve with findings=[]. Bounded: no fifth guard shape is proposed.

findings.description: The coverage document overstates its own coverage: it promises a mechanical self-maintenance property that no longer exists, so a maintainer adding a new producer would believe the file catches it automatically when the enumeration is in fact hand-maintained (the 3.2 removal note says exactly this at lines 860-866). This is the same stale-3.2 defect class as the header Sections: entry round 5 DID fix, missed by an incomplete sweep - the 0ggk failure shape recurring inside the deliverable that documents it. Fix is comment-only and moves no pins: rewrite the two banner passages to past tense pointing at the 3.2 removal note, and drop or qualify 'THE FULL CONTRIBUTOR SET... verified by reading the call graph'.

findings.evidence: assert_absent is invoked at line 1270 (assertion 4.6b) but never defined in this self-contained spec - it exists only as local copies in three sibling specs (runner-completeness:92, override-disclosure:129, gate-claim-honesty:257), none of which this file sources. Measured on a live run: the output contains 'line 1270: assert_absent: command not found'; 4.6b neither passes nor fails (output shows 4.6a, the error, then 4.6c); the suite still prints '149 passed, 0 failed' and exits 0. The spec therefore has 150 WRITTEN assertions of which 149 execute, and the recorded '149/0' acceptance figure silently includes a check that structurally cannot run. Fix verified in a scratchpad copy: inserting gate-claim-honesty.test.sh:257's assert_absent verbatim yields 150 passed / 0 failed with 4.6b PASS - so the asserted property (M6 carries no Reused-because line) does hold in shipped text, nothing was masked, and no sha256 pin moves.
findings.description: A shipped assertion in the release gate's own regression guard that cannot execute - emitting an unread 'command not found' into every run since round 4 - is a live instance of the defect family this task exists to repair: a check that claims to check and does not. It survived four independent review rounds and the round-4/round-5 'confirmed identical' output diff (the error line was identical on both sides, so the diff could not surface it). Fix: add the local assert_absent definition (drop-in), re-run standalone, and record the corrected floor as 150/0 wherever 149/0 is cited going forward.
